Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All motors are ships.

Some ships are bowls.

No ship is a hammer.

**Conclusions:**

(I) Some motors are hammers.

(II) Some bowls are motors.

(III) Some bowls are not hammers.

options.text: Either conclusion I or conclusion III follows
All the conclusions I, II and III follow

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4011cff0d58a65754abde889719be830d801cb10a130f6c751aa3214cc69b6e8.png] 

Conclusions:

(I) Some motors are hammers → **False** (All motors are ships, and no ship is hammer implies that no motor is hammer).

(II) Some bowls are motors → **False** (All motors are ships, and some ships are bowls implies that some bowls can be motors. This is possible but not definite).

(III) Some bowls are not hammers → **True** (All motors are ships, some ships are bowls, and no ship is a hammer implies that some bowls which are ships are not hammer).

Hence, the correct answer is **"****Only conclusion III follows"**.

questions.question: Under which Schedule of the Indian Constitution is the form of oath or affirmation for a Judge of the Supreme Court mentioned?

__
 
• The form of oath or affirmation for a Judge of the Supreme Court is mentioned in the **Third Schedule** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Third Schedule also includes forms of oath or affirmation for other constitutional positions such as the President, Vice-President, Ministers, Members of Parliament, and Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.
 
• Taking an oath or affirmation is a mandatory requirement before assuming office for these constitutional positions.
 
• The oath or affirmation signifies the commitment to uphold the Constitution and discharge duties faithfully and impartially.

• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.

questions.question: In a 150-m race, if R gets a 5-metre head start, then he would beat S by 35 metres. If S gets a 25-metre head start in a 100-metre race, then _______ would win the race by ________ metres.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

In a 150-metre race, R gets a 5-metre head start and beats S by 35 metres.

**Formula used:**

Let the speed of R be r and the speed of S be s.

Time taken by R to run 145 metres = Time taken by S to run 115 metres

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

145 / r = 115 / s

⇒ r / s = 145 / 115 = 29 / 23

In a 100-metre race, S gets a 25-metre head start:

So, R runs 100 metres and S runs 75 metres.

Let the time taken by R be tR and time taken by S be tS.

tR = 100 / r

tS = 75 / s

Using the speed ratio r/s = 29/23:

tS = 75 / s = 75 / (23r/29)

⇒ tS = 75 × (29 / 23r)

⇒ tS = (75 × 29) / (23 × r)

⇒ tS = (2175) / (23r)

Comparing tR and tS:

tR = 100 / r

tS = 2175 / (23r)

⇒ 100 / r > 2175 / (23r)

⇒ 100 > 2175 / 23

⇒ 100 > 94.57

Therefore, S finishes the 75 meters first. To find by how much S wins:

Distance covered by R when S finishes:

tS = 75 / s

Distance covered by R in this time:

D = r × tS = r × (75 / s)

Using r/s = 29/23:

D = r × (75 / (23r/29)) = 75 × (29 / 23)

D = 75 × (29 / 23) = 75 × 1.26 = 94.56

Therefore, R covers 94.56 meters when S finishes 75 meters.

Remaining distance for R:

100 - 94.56 = 5.44 meters

**∴ The correct answer is S, winning by 5.44 meters.**
